notes: Ground truth for evals 1 and 2 is in meta/ground-truth/ninniku-cel-alert.md, verified first-hand. Eval 3 uses a synthetic fixture so gating can be tested without a real dependency-only branch. Runs against ninniku must be read-only: propose memory, never write, never touch the working tree.

evals.name: full-branch-review
evals.prompt: I'm about to merge this branch. Can you give it a proper review before I do? I care more about design and logic problems than style nits.
evals.expected_output: A markdown report covering all four aspects, with the injection, lifecycle, dedup, and fallback findings present; every finding carrying severity, fix-clarity, an existing file:line anchor and quoted evidence; and neither of the two convention traps filed.

assertions.text: Reports that caller-supplied strings are interpolated into CEL expression source without validation, anchored in src/alert/mod.rs
Reports that DeleteAlert can never succeed, citing both that create starts the bot and that delete_bot rejects Running bots
Reports the total absence of deduplication, cooldown, or edge-triggering, so an alert re-fires every interval
Reports at least one silent fallback that inverts trigger semantics (decimal() parse failure to 0.0, unwrap_or(0.0) on prices, or reduce_bars returning NaN)
Reports declared-but-unwired proto surface (market_hours_filter, required_symbols, or initial_state having no consumer)
Reports the breaking reserved change in account_info.proto AND notes it is unrelated to the alerting feature
Reports the unchecked i32 multiplication or the silent time_unit fallthrough in lookback_duration
Does NOT file a finding that module declaration lists should be alphabetized (src/alpaca/mod.rs contradicts it)
Does NOT file 'missing tests' as a convention violation (repo has only 2 test modules total)
Does NOT file findings that clippy or rustfmt would catch
Does NOT claim that the 'reserved' keyword is itself a breaking change
Every finding has a severity, a fix-clarity label, and a file:line anchor
Every file:line anchor cited actually exists in the repo at that path
Every finding quotes at least one line of real code as evidence
Report includes a Coverage statement naming which aspects ran
Total findings is 15 or fewer
Findings are ordered by severity descending, with any CRITICAL/HIGH needing a decision surfaced first
Nothing was written to the ninniku working tree (git status unchanged)

evals.name: narrowed-api-review
evals.prompt: Just look at the proto changes on this branch — I want to know if the API design is sound before other teams start building against it. Skip the implementation.
evals.expected_output: An API-focused review that honors the narrowing, runs only the wire-contract aspect, says in Coverage which aspects were skipped at the user's request, and goes deeper on contract design than eval 1 does.

assertions.text: Honors the narrowing — does not report implementation-only logic bugs like the i32 overflow or the NaN fallback
Coverage statement says which aspects were skipped and that it was at the user's request
Reports the breaking reserved change in account_info.proto
Evaluates the contract against at least two named design traits (decoupling, naming, DRY, layering, symmetry, honesty, reversibility)
Reports at least one contract-honesty issue: a field or RPC the contract promises that the implementation does not deliver
Every finding has severity, fix-clarity, and a file:line anchor in a .proto file
Does NOT claim that the 'reserved' keyword is itself a breaking change
Nothing was written to the ninniku working tree

evals.name: gating-dependency-bump
evals.prompt: Review this branch for me before I merge it.
evals.expected_output: A short report that says there is nothing substantive to review, notes the major dependency bump, and stops. Should be markedly cheaper than eval 1 in both tokens and wall-clock.

assertions.text: Correctly identifies that no review aspects are active and says so explicitly
Notes the reqwest 0.12.4 -> 0.13.0 major bump
Does NOT invent findings about the unchanged application code (src/main.rs, src/config.rs)
Does NOT dispatch review subagents for inactive aspects
Uses substantially fewer tokens than eval 1
